issues.legal_issue: Income derived from selling milk from cattle maintained by a family is not agricultural income for assessment under agricultural income-tax law.
material_facts: The joint family maintained cows and buffaloes and received income from selling their milk.
The assessment included income from milk sales, but the Tribunal excluded it as non-agricultural income.
The High Court affirmed that treatment, and the State did not challenge the answer to this issue before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court treated the issue as concluded by its earlier decision and did not disturb the finding that the milk-sale income was not agricultural income.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that the question was concluded by Commissioner of Income-tax, West Bengal, Calcutta v. Raja Benoy Kumar Sahas Roy, [1958] SCR 101. The judgment does not restate that decision’s reasoning.

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_assessment: A person or family is assessed under a tax system that applies to agricultural income.
predicates.milk_income_from_cattle_kept_by_the_fami: A family receives income from selling milk produced by cattle it maintains.

issues.definition: When an agricultural-income tax assessment includes income from milk produced by a family’s cattle, the income is treated as non-agricultural.

issues.legal_issue: A joint Hindu family composed only of brothers and the specified close relatives of brothers qualifies as a family consisting of brothers only for the purpose of the scheduled tax rates.
material_facts: The assessee represented a joint Hindu family comprising the sons of two deceased brothers.
The family owned agricultural land and its members were the sons of those deceased brothers.
The Act’s Schedule defined “brother” to include a brother’s son, a brother’s son’s son, and a brother’s widow.
The Tribunal granted the family the benefit of the Schedule’s rates, and the High Court affirmed that treatment.
issues.conclusion: The family was to be treated as consisting of brothers only and was entitled to the benefit of the rates in the Schedule.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(1) of the Orissa Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1947, a Hindu undivided family’s agricultural income was generally treated as the income of one individual, but the proviso allowed the scheduled rates for a family consisting of brothers only. Clause B of the Schedule prescribed those rates. The Schedule’s Explanation defined “brother” to include a brother’s son, a brother’s son’s son, and a brother’s widow. The Court incorporated that Explanation into the phrase “consisting of brothers only,” so a family of the sons of deceased brothers came within the phrase.

predicates.joint_hindu_family_tax_assessment: A joint Hindu family’s income is being assessed for tax.
predicates.all_members_are_brothers_or_brothers_son: Every family member is a brother or is a brother’s son, a brother’s son’s son, or a brother’s widow.

issues.definition: If a joint Hindu family is being assessed and all its members fall within those stated family relationships, the family qualifies for the special scheduled rates.
